newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher, Elbit Systems soars.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher, Elbit Systems soars.

text.p: Israeli shares closed up on Thursday in volatile trading spurred by speculation in index options, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.43 percent, or 0.85 points, to 198.92 on a fairly high all-share turnover of 93 million shekels against 62 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.47 percent to 208.95.
"The most active players were Maof options speculators who were trying to push up the market ahead of the expiry of November options today," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"The mood in the market has improved lately but it is still too early to talk about a positive trend. It's very difficult to predict where the market is going," Scharia added.

"The Maof players were rocking the market today. They were pushing the Maof index to 209.31 in the Meretz (morning session). Even arbitrage shares (which are also traded in the United States) that declined on Wednesday in New York were rising," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"After the expiry of the options the market started falling, closing with only a moderate gain," she added.

Elbit Ltd completed its spin-off on Thursday with its break-up into three publicly traded companies. On its first day of trading Elbit Systems, the most active share, soared 207.75 percent to 2,268 on volume of 8.8 million shekels after rising a similar amount on Nasdaq overnight.
Elbit Medical Imaging plunged 42.25 percent to 1,254 and Elbit fell 10 percent to 3,204. Traders said the opening price of the shares did not reflect their real value.

Bank Hapoalim, the third most active share, fell 2.0 percent to 479 on volume of 4.6 million shekels after reporting third-quarter net profit of 262.7 million shekels against 189.2 million a year earlier. Traders said the results were already reflected in the share's price.
IDB Holdings rose 1.0 percent to 1,201 despite reporting a third-quarter net loss of 5.3 million shekels against net profit of 40.2 million shekels a year earlier.

IDB's subsidiary IDB Development Corp gained 1.5 percent to 5,575 after reporting a third-quarter net loss of 3.6 million shekels against net profit of 58.7 million shekels a year earlier. Traders said the results of both companies were within expectations and were reflected in their price.
Osem Investments gained 2.25 percent to 1,808 after reporting third-quarter net profit rose to 20.7 million shekels from 17.8 million a year earlier.
Koor Industries, the second most active share, gained 0.25 to 28,162 on volume of 4.7 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 ($1 = 3.26 shekels)
